assumptions_challenged: That supplying the MISEV2023 guideline alone is sufficient to evaluate program-specific compliance or noncompliance with CMC/analytics expectations.
That absence of program documents in the reviewed dataset reliably indicates the program does not hold (or cannot produce) those documents.
That community guidance (MISEV2023) can be treated as direct evidence that the program must already meet all enumerated controls prior to any further interpretation of provided program data.

That rodent intranasal biodistribution observations are nontranslatable for this specific program absent validated intact-EV assays, even though no program biodistribution or assay data were presented to test translatability for SGL-001.
falsification_conditions: Provide program-specific MCB/WCB documentation showing identity testing (STR), mycoplasma results, defined passage limits and seed lot control — demonstrating the program holds controlled source-cell banking.

Provide validated intact-EV analytical method reports (including LLOQ, specificity, precision, accuracy) and orthogonal QC panel SOPs/release specifications demonstrating the assays are fit-for-purpose for SGL-001.
Provide a stability-indicating potency assay validation and data linking that assay to an in vivo PD endpoint (with raw data and analysis) for SGL-001.
Provide records of three GMP-like production runs with release, stability, and comparability data showing reproducible lot-to-lot performance for the intranasal formulation.

Provide program-specific rodent and at least one larger-animal intranasal biodistribution data set generated using the validated intact-EV assays, with controls to show signal derives from vesicles rather than non-vesicular particles.
strongest_objection: The reviewers treat the absence of program-specific CMC, assay validation, and biodistribution records in the supplied dataset as a basis to assert those program elements are unsupported, but they also generalize MISEV2023 guidance into program requirements without demonstrating that the program actually lacks or fails those requirements. In short: conclusions hinge on 'absence of supplied records' rather than on affirmative, program-linked evidence, so the reviewers risk conflating missing evidence with verified program deficiency.
